resources.string: Works offline. Times are calculated on this phone.
Next stage: fonts, colours, sizes, numerals, icons, layout, saved themes and a separate Always-On design, with a live preview, sent to the watch as a new version of the Noor face.
On: checks every few hours using low-power location
Off: updates when you open the app or the time zone changes
Add or subtract minutes for each time
Prayer times for where you are
Noor uses your approximate location to calculate prayer times and choose the right authority, such as IACAD in Dubai. Your location stays on this phone; it is never uploaded.
Keep times right when you travel
To update automatically when you are not using the app, Android needs “Allow all the time”. Noor checks rarely, with low-power location, so battery use is minimal. You can turn this off at any time.
Location permission not granted. Choose a city or allow location in system settings.
Wear OS services are not available on this phone. Install the Galaxy Wearable app and pair your watch.
Could not hand the settings to Wear OS. Try again.

The Noor watch app calculates the same times as this phone, with the same location, authority and adjustments, and keeps working without the phone. It adds a “Prayer times” tile and a “Next prayer” complication you can put on any watch face.
Set your location to find the Qibla.
This phone has no compass sensor. Use the bearing below with a separate compass.
You are within a few kilometres of the Kaaba. Face the Masjid al-Haram directly; a compass is not precise this close.
You are near the point opposite Makkah: almost every direction is nearly equally short. The bearing shown is the great-circle one.
Lay it face up, level, for an accurate reading.
The phone estimates its heading is within ±%1$s°.
The magnetic field here is unusual: metal or a magnet nearby is disturbing the compass.
The compass needs calibrating: tap for how.
Based on the sensor status reported by the phone. Tap for calibration tips.
Directions are true north. Qibla is the shortest path on the Earth\'s ellipsoid (WGS-84) to the Kaaba. Two decimals are shown; the real accuracy is the sensor\'s, shown above.
Move away from metal, electronics, speakers and car interiors.
Take the phone out of any case or holder with a magnet.
Hold the phone and trace a figure eight in the air a few times, turning your wrist.
Then rotate the phone slowly a full turn while keeping it flat.
Lay it flat and wait a few seconds for the reading to settle.
Pair your Galaxy Watch with the Galaxy Wearable app (or another Wear OS watch with its companion app), keep Bluetooth on, then come back here.
The watch did not answer. Make sure it is connected and awake, then try again.
The Play Store is open on your watch. Tap Install there; this page updates by itself when it is done.
Not installed yet. If the Play Store page closed, open it again.

This is a development build, not from Google Play, so the watch app is installed separately (see the guide). Once Noor is on Google Play, this button opens the watch\'s Play Store for a one-tap install.
Opens Noor in the Play Store on your watch: one tap there installs it.
Open Play Store on watch again

Official timetable: %1$s\'s own times for this date, as published.
Calculated with %1$s\'s conventions, checked against its official timetable.
Calculated with the parameters %1$s is documented to use; not yet checked against its own timetable.

Precise: neighbourhood names, best Qibla bearing
Approximate: town names only. Change in Android settings.
Official timetable where published; validated calculation otherwise

Official timetables: IACAD Dubai (iacad.gov.ae; 2021–2023 pages preserved by the Internet Archive, November 2026 from the IACAD website); MUIS Singapore 2024–2026 (data.gov.sg, Singapore Open Data Licence). Place names: GeoNames (geonames.org), CC BY 4.0. Magnetic declination: World Magnetic Model, via Android. Each authority\'s parameters and their sources are listed in docs/AUTHORITIES.md in the Noor repository.
